paragraphs: Sum-product circuits offer compact ways to represent information such as logical functions and probability distributions. Their structure can make some inference questions efficient to answer. This paper asks how to understand efficiency when a more complicated question combines several operations, rather than fitting a single familiar query type.

The authors describe these combinations through an algebraic framework based on semirings. They express a broad collection of queries using three building blocks: aggregation, multiplication, and elementwise mapping. The examples include marginal MAP inference, inference in probabilistic answer set programs, and causal backdoor adjustment. Putting these problems into a shared language makes their computational requirements easier to analyze together.

The main results give sufficient conditions under which compositions remain tractable. These conditions concern both circuit structure, including marginal determinism and compatibility, and the mappings applied to circuit values. They establish circumstances that guarantee efficient inference, without claiming to characterize every tractable case. The framework recovers existing results, derives new conditions, and supplies a reusable approach for analyzing additional combinations of inference operations.
neurips-2024-a-compositional-atlas-for-a.tldr: An algebraic framework unifies inference queries on circuits and gives sufficient conditions for their efficient composition.

paragraphs: Pruning reduces the size of a language model by removing weights, but deciding which weights to remove is only part of the problem. Different layers can warrant different amounts of pruning. This paper introduces DSA, an automated framework that searches for rules assigning sparsity levels across layers, addressing performance losses associated with less adaptive allocation.

DSA builds an allocation rule in two stages. It first combines individual weight metrics into an importance score for each layer, then converts those scores into sparsity ratios. The search space includes preprocessing, reduction, transformation, and postprocessing operations. An evolutionary algorithm evaluates candidate rules and creates new candidates by combining and modifying promising ones.

The discovered rules can be incorporated into existing methods that use uniform sparsity allocation. Experiments report significant gains across arithmetic, knowledge reasoning, and multimodal tasks using several language-model families. For LLaMA-1, LLaMA-2, and LLaMA-3, the abstract reports gains of 4.73%, 6.18%, and 10.65% over state-of-the-art techniques. These findings support treating the allocation rule itself as an important part of model compression.
neurips-2024-discovering-sparsity-alloca.tldr: DSA searches for layer-specific pruning rules that improve the performance of compressed language models.

paragraphs: DynaMITE-RL addresses reinforcement learning in environments whose hidden state changes at varying rates. An agent must infer information it cannot directly observe while learning how to act. The paper focuses on how meta-reinforcement learning can organize that inference when relevant hidden information stays stable for part of an episode and then changes.

The approach divides an episode conceptually into sessions, each defined as a period with a fixed latent state. It introduces three modifications to existing meta-RL methods: consistency of latent information within a session, session masking, and conditioning on prior latent information. Together, these changes give the inference process an explicit way to account for the session structure of the environment.

The authors evaluate the approach in discrete Gridworld environments, continuous-control problems, and simulated robot assistance tasks. They report that the modifications matter and that DynaMITE-RL performs effectively against state-of-the-art baselines in both online and offline reinforcement learning. The findings support modeling periods of latent stability when adapting to environments that change over time.
neurips-2024-dynamite-rl-a-dynamic-model.tldr: DynaMITE-RL improves adaptation by explicitly modeling periods during which an environment’s hidden state remains fixed.

paragraphs: Differentially private systems often measure some queries privately and reconstruct other answers from those measurements. This reconstruction step matters because it helps systems use their privacy budget economically while controlling error and handling datasets with many dimensions. The paper develops methods for reconstructing marginal queries, which summarize selected subsets of data attributes.

The first method, ReM, converts residual measurements into marginal answers through a principled, efficient postprocessing procedure. It builds on a residual query basis with an efficiently computable pseudoinverse, a mathematical operation used to recover answers from measurements. The contribution therefore targets a reusable reconstruction step within private query-answering mechanisms.

The extension GReM-LNN addresses measurements affected by Gaussian noise. It reconstructs marginals while enforcing consistency and non-negativity, so the reconstructed answers agree with one another and do not contain negative values. These constraints often reduce reconstruction error, rather than guaranteeing an improvement in every instance. Applications to existing private query-answering mechanisms demonstrate the practical utility of both methods and show how improved postprocessing can strengthen larger privacy-preserving systems.
neurips-2024-efficient-and-private-margi.tldr: ReM and GReM-LNN efficiently reconstruct private marginal answers, with consistency and non-negativity often reducing error under Gaussian noise.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization places one optimization problem inside another. Algorithms for these problems often require Hessian computations, which become costly in high dimensions. This paper develops first-order methods for problems with linear constraints, extending a direction previously explored mainly for unconstrained settings. It provides finite-time guarantees for reaching specified forms of stationarity.

For linear equality constraints, the methods reach epsilon-stationarity using approximately epsilon to the power of minus two gradient-oracle calls, with logarithmic factors suppressed. The authors characterize this rate as nearly optimal. For linear inequality constraints, they obtain a Goldstein stationarity guarantee with complexity approximately d times delta to the power of minus one times epsilon to the power of minus three, where d is the upper-level dimension.

A second inequality-constrained result removes the dimension dependence, but requires oracle access to the optimal dual variable and has an epsilon-to-the-minus-four dependence. That additional access assumption is essential to the stated dimension-free guarantee. The work also develops methods for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization with inexact oracles, and reports numerical experiments supporting the theoretical guarantees.
neurips-2024-first-order-methods-for-lin.tldr: First-order methods provide finite-time stationarity guarantees for bilevel problems with linear constraints, including a conditional dimension-free result.

paragraphs: ImOV3D studies whether a detector can learn from only two-dimensional images and then identify objects in three-dimensional point clouds, including categories beyond those labeled during training. This setup addresses the shortage of annotated 3D data by drawing on the richer supply of annotated images. The central obstacle is that training images and test-time point clouds present information in different forms.

The framework creates a shared representation containing both an image and a point cloud. It estimates depth from a single image to construct 3D information, and renders 3D scenes to obtain images. These conversions bring training and testing into a common format that combines visual semantics with depth and spatial structure. The conversions are designed to reduce the mismatch between the two settings.

Experiments on SUNRGBD and ScanNet report significant improvements over existing methods without ground-truth 3D training data. Adding a small amount of real 3D data for fine-tuning also significantly exceeds the previous state of the art. The findings support the usefulness of this shared representation for transferring image-based knowledge into 3D detection.
neurips-2024-imov3d-learning-open-vocabu.tldr: ImOV3D learns open-vocabulary 3D detection from 2D images by converting images and point clouds into a shared multimodal representation.

paragraphs: Approximate Personalized PageRank is a local graph algorithm whose runtime bound does not depend on the size of the whole graph. This paper observes that it is also a local version of the Gauss-Seidel iterative solver. That connection motivates a broader question: can other standard iterative methods concentrate their work on locally active parts of a graph?

The authors introduce a locally evolving set process to describe and analyze this behavior. The framework tracks active-node volume and the residual ratio over the computation. It yields a new runtime bound for Approximate Personalized PageRank that reflects these evolving quantities, connecting the analysis more closely to actual computational work. It also shows that many standard solvers can be localized.

For a local Chebyshev method, the faster runtime guarantee is conditional on the geometric mean of residual reduction scaling as the square root of the damping factor. The result does not require a monotonicity assumption. Numerical experiments on real-world graphs show efficiency gains, including speedups of up to one hundred times over corresponding standard solvers.
neurips-2024-iterative-methods-via-local.tldr: A framework for localizing iterative solvers yields refined runtime bounds and substantial empirical speedups on graph problems.

paragraphs: Neural Embeddings Rank, or NER, seeks a compact representation of neural activity that aligns with movement. It maps neural dynamics into three dimensions and contrasts those embeddings using movement ranks. This connects continuous neural representations to continuous movements while producing a space that can be directly visualized.

The researchers compare NER with six other dimensionality reduction techniques using recordings from three cortical areas while monkeys perform reaching tasks. Among the tested methods, only NER aligns the latent dynamics with both hand position and direction. It also reveals consistent dynamics in primary motor and dorsal premotor cortex across sixteen sessions spanning a year.

A linear decoder using NER explains 86% of velocity variance and 97% of position variance. Models trained on one session also decode velocity, position, and direction in held-out data from other dates and cortical areas. NER additionally reveals distinct patterns in somatosensory cortex during consistent movements and in motor cortex during curved reaches. These results show that the representation can expose both shared and differing relationships between neural activity and movement.
neurips-2024-neural-embeddings-rank-alig.tldr: NER creates three-dimensional neural representations aligned with movement and supports decoding across recording sessions and cortical areas.

paragraphs: Hypothesis selection chooses a distribution from a finite list using samples from an unknown distribution. The goal is to select a candidate whose total variation distance from the truth is close to that of the best available candidate. The guarantee has two parts: a multiplicative factor on the best candidate’s error and a small additive error.

The paper gives the first almost-linear-time algorithm achieving multiplicative factor three. Its runtime is approximately n divided by epsilon cubed, with logarithmic factors suppressed, where n is the number of candidates and epsilon is the additive accuracy parameter. Earlier algorithms required more time, accepted a worse multiplicative factor, or imposed additional assumptions.

The significance of three comes from a lower bound: achieving a smaller factor can require samples proportional to the distribution’s domain size, even with only two candidates. The result therefore combines the optimal factor in that sense with almost-linear dependence on candidate count. A second algorithm improves the dependence on additive accuracy while accepting factor four, offering a different trade-off between runtime and approximation quality.
neurips-2024-optimal-hypothesis-selectio.tldr: A new hypothesis-selection algorithm achieves approximation factor three in almost-linear time in the number of candidate distributions.

paragraphs: This paper explores how AI might carry cultural knowledge forward while allowing it to change. The authors call this Artificial Authentic Intelligence, framing authenticity as a relationship between preserving a tradition and creating new expression. Their case study concerns Thai traditional dance and how its underlying knowledge can inform human-machine collaboration.

They implement the idea in Cyber Subin, a system for real-time co-dancing, and Open Dance Lab, an educational website. Both translate the 59 foundational poses of Mae Bot Yai into six generative principles derived from choreographer Pichet Klunchun’s analysis. Rule-based AI uses those principles to support new expressions grounded in the dance tradition.

The evaluation considers three dimensions of authenticity: embodied knowledge transfer, community validation, and communication across cultures. The authors interpret their findings as showing that cultural authenticity can emerge through the creative tension between inherited knowledge and algorithmic expression. The contribution is a concrete exploration of how cultural AI can work through generative principles and collaborative practice, with authenticity assessed through relationships to knowledge, communities, and audiences.
neurips-2025-artificial-authentic-intell.tldr: Two Thai dance systems explore how rule-based AI can preserve cultural knowledge while supporting new, collaboratively created expressions.

paragraphs: Artism proposes an AI architecture for exploring possible directions in the evolution of art. Its organizing idea is to connect artistic generation with critical analysis, allowing the two activities to participate in an interactive process. The paper presents this as a methodology for investigating artistic concepts and their potential development.

The architecture has two connected components. AIDA is an artificial artist social network, while the Ismism Machine supplies critical analysis. Deep learning and collaboration among multiple agents support simulations of art-historical developments and patterns of conceptual innovation. Bringing these components together creates a framework for critical loops in which artistic activity and reflection are linked.

The authors describe the approach as a move toward reflexive practice: creation can be considered alongside an ongoing process of critique. They are applying the method in experimental studies of contemporary art concepts. The stated contribution is therefore an emerging general methodology and its architectural proposal, with possibilities for computational art analysis. The abstract presents these possibilities without claiming that the system has established which future artistic trajectories will occur.
neurips-2025-artism-ai-driven-dual-engin.tldr: Artism connects an artificial artist network with a critique system to explore artistic development through interactive critical loops.

paragraphs: This project uses generative AI to reinterpret the soundscape of Ming Dynasty sacrificial rituals at the Temple of Heaven. Its artistic focus is how spiritual perception and cultural memory can be reshaped through an encounter between historical materials and ambiguous machine-generated imagery and sound. Historical reconstruction provides a grounding for the experience.

The work combines ritual texts, spatial models, and restored music with blurred, changing audiovisual material generated by AI. A three-screen interactive installation brings together the traditional soundscape information, generated hallucinations, and a ritual timeline. Audience participation can influence the hallucinations in real time, making the experience responsive to the people engaging with it.

The project explicitly pursues an imaginative interpretation rather than historical reproduction. The instability of generative AI becomes part of its artistic method, creating tension between archival rigor and uncertain perception. The installation uses that tension to explore sacred atmosphere, individual experience, and collective imagination. Its contribution is an approach to cultural heritage art in which reconstructed evidence and synthetic memory remain visibly intertwined.
neurips-2025-between-reality-and-ai-hall.tldr: An interactive installation combines reconstructed Ming ritual soundscapes with AI hallucinations to explore cultural memory and spiritual experience.

paragraphs: CoTextor is a framework for editing multilingual text inside images while giving users control over the process. The task involves more than changing words: the edited text must also fit the surrounding picture. The framework makes these parts of the workflow explicit and supports reversible edits, so users can guide and revisit individual operations.

The process separates foreground extraction, background repair, semantic rewriting, and depth-aware reintegration. Users can rotate, move, resize, and warp content. A perceptually guided integration module improves how reinserted text matches the image’s appearance and geometry. This layered structure connects control over the wording with control over the text’s visual placement.

CoTextor uses publicly available pretrained components and requires no retraining or annotation. The authors demonstrate it through poster localization, street art remixing, and educational content creation. These scenarios show how a modular editing workflow can support visual storytelling across languages and cultural settings. The emphasis is on accessible human-AI co-creation, with users able to direct both the meaning and presentation of edited text.
neurips-2025-cotextor-training-free-modu.tldr: CoTextor enables controllable multilingual text editing in images through reversible layers built from pretrained components.

paragraphs: Craving Checkpoint explores how an AI-enabled physical object might encourage reflection at the moment someone accesses food. It takes the form of an interactive fridge lock and is designed as a just-in-time adaptive intervention. Its purpose is to make the immediate eating decision a moment of awareness and dialogue.

The system asks users about mood and hunger, then responds through a humanlike voice and coordinated lighting. A large language model personalizes suggestions using the user’s state and behavioral patterns. These elements combine a physical interaction with emotionally expressive feedback, placing the exchange within the act of approaching food.

Although the object is a fridge lock, the described interaction aims to guide choices gently without enforcing control. The paper presents food access as a shared ritual in which the user and system shape the exchange together. This is a design exploration of timely, personalized support for mindful eating and sustainable behavior change. Its stated contribution concerns how such support can be embodied in an everyday object; the abstract does not establish lasting dietary outcomes.
neurips-2025-craving-checkpoint-an-inter.tldr: Craving Checkpoint uses a conversational fridge interface to encourage mindful reflection and personalized guidance at the moment of food access.

paragraphs: Gaze to the Stars is a participatory artwork that uses the MIT Great Dome as a surface for collective emotional storytelling. The project brings personal reflection into a shared public setting through conversations with AI and large-scale projection. Its focus is the relationship between an individual’s feelings and emotions shared across a group.

Two hundred participants engage in reflective conversations with a large language model. Their responses are encoded in Braille within videos of their irises, and the resulting material is projected onto the Dome. The system combines affective narrative embedding, iris segmentation, and emotional clustering to represent personal accounts alongside patterns of shared feeling.

The artwork connects a conversational encounter with an intimate bodily image and a public architectural display. That combination gives the project its approach to moving between personal and collective experience. The authors frame AI as a companion that invites reflection and civic empathy. The contribution is an artistic realization of that framing: a public installation organized around emotional expression, participation, and the visibility of shared experience.
neurips-2025-gaze-to-the-stars-ai-and-pu.tldr: Gaze to the Stars turns AI-guided personal reflections and iris videos into a public installation about shared emotion.

paragraphs: witheFlow explores collaboration between musicians and machines through real-time control of audio effects. The paper starts from the role of emotion in human performance and uses that setting to consider how a computational system can participate. The proposed contribution is a responsive effects system designed to accompany the performer’s activity.

The system extracts features from both biosignals and the audio being produced. It uses those features to modulate audio effects automatically during performance. Connecting these two sources of information makes the performer’s bodily signals and the sounding music inputs to the same interaction. The design links human expression to changes in the treatment of sound.

The project is currently a proof of concept. It is intended to be lightweight enough to run locally on a laptop, and its open-source setup requires compatible sensors and a Digital Audio Workstation. These practical requirements define the setting in which the proposed interaction operates. The work presents a way to explore emotionally responsive musical collaboration, with the musician’s experience supplying the human side of that relationship.
neurips-2025-go-witheflow-real-time-emot.tldr: witheFlow is a proof-of-concept system that uses biosignals and audio features to adjust musical effects during live performance.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to identify themes in Nigerian lyrics when electricity and computing resources are limited. Its corpus includes English, Yoruba, and Nigerian Pidgin, retaining code-switching and devotional language to preserve cultural nuance. The evaluation treats energy consumption as a practical consideration alongside the quality and distinctness of the discovered topics.

The authors compare seven topic models using coherence, topic diversity, overlap, and direct energy measurements. NMF achieves the best coherence among the classical models, with a Cv score of 0.6045 at about 0.000002 kWh. LSI also combines low energy use with competitive quality. BERTopic produces maximal diversity and no measured topic overlap, but uses substantially more energy.

Other results reinforce that greater energy use does not automatically produce better topics: Top2Vec has lower coherence, while GSDMM has undefined coherence on this short, sparse corpus and the highest energy consumption. The authors recommend classical methods, particularly NMF, as a starting point in resource-constrained contexts, reserving more energy-intensive approaches for needs such as stronger topical separation.
neurips-2025-green-topics-deep-roots-ene.tldr: A comparison on multilingual Nigerian lyrics finds that classical topic models, especially NMF, offer a strong quality-energy trade-off.

paragraphs: This paper develops a way for robots to acquire new movement styles from a few videos of human movement. It starts with existing human-robot dance collaborations and adapts their motion to additional styles. The goal is to expand a robot’s expressive range while retaining the underlying trajectory of the original choreography.

A dual-stream architecture processes both raw video frames and pose sequences. Cross-modal attention connects these sources to capture rhythm, acceleration patterns, and spatial coordination. A transformer then learns residual motion transformations, allowing adaptation from three to six demonstration videos. A creativity parameter controls the balance between stronger stylistic changes and preservation of the original trajectory.

The evaluation covers ballet, jazz, flamenco, contemporary dance, and martial arts. The authors report successful differentiation among styles, with overall style-transfer scores increasing by factors of 6.7 to 7.4 between minimum and maximum creativity settings. Those gains describe the effect of changing that control. The framework provides a means of shaping robot motion expressively through limited demonstrations and an adjustable style-trajectory trade-off.
neurips-2025-learning-to-move-with-style.tldr: A video-and-pose framework transfers movement styles to robot choreography from three to six demonstrations with adjustable creative intensity.

paragraphs: This paper connects large language models to Grasshopper through the Model Context Protocol, allowing designers to develop parametric 3D models conversationally. The system translates creative instructions into structured operations on design components. Its purpose is to make architectural and landscape modeling workflows accessible through language while retaining the structure of parametric design.

A client-server architecture parses natural-language instructions into commands that invoke modular components. Designers can prompt, revise, and refine models through this interface. Domain knowledge is encoded in design lexicons, giving the conversational system a set of specialized components and relationships through which to express a user’s intent.

The system was demonstrated in a nine-day workshop involving twenty participants in five teams. Each team created a distinct lexicon, covering areas such as generative open spaces and urban functional zoning, which novices could subsequently operate using language. The authors also describe how the protocol supports combining components from different workflows. The workshop observations illustrate expanded access to specialized design knowledge and the potential for composing previously separate modeling practices.
neurips-2025-mcp-driven-parametric-model.tldr: An MCP integration lets language models operate Grasshopper components so designers can create and refine parametric models conversationally.

paragraphs: Music Arena is an open platform for comparing text-to-music systems through human listening preferences. Listening studies are valuable, but separate studies can be costly and difficult to compare when their procedures differ. The platform brings these judgments into a shared, ongoing evaluation process driven by prompts chosen by real users.

Users listen to outputs from two systems and indicate their preferences, which contribute to a leaderboard. The platform includes an LLM-based routing system to accommodate differences in the kinds of inputs and outputs supported by music generators. It also gathers listening data and written feedback, adding detail beyond a single preference choice.

The authors propose a rolling release of preference data with user privacy guarantees. This would provide a renewable resource that could help researchers align music generators or improve automatic evaluation metrics. The contribution combines a standardized comparison procedure with music-specific routing and richer feedback collection. It shows how live evaluation can be adapted to a domain where listening behavior and the diversity of generation interfaces both matter.
neurips-2025-music-arena-live-evaluation.tldr: Music Arena gathers live listener comparisons of text-to-music systems to support a shared leaderboard and renewable preference data.

paragraphs: This paper examines a role for generative AI centered on supporting the human creative process. The authors raise the possibility that handing primary responsibility for making an artifact to AI may change that process in undesirable ways. They explore what assistance could look like when the person continues to lead the creative work.

Their proposed role is an AI muse: a conversational partner that offers encouragement, constructive feedback, and reflection that broadens the creator’s perspective. Substantial content generation remains available when requested. This arrangement makes the kind and timing of assistance central to the interaction, with support extending beyond the production of finished material.

The authors first review the roles played by human muses, then discuss interactions with several generative AI models across three use scenarios. From these interactions, they identify conversational behaviors an AI muse would need. The contribution is a way to think about and characterize creative assistance, emphasizing how dialogue can sustain human participation and help creators explore their own work.
neurips-2025-musings-on-ai-muses-support.tldr: The paper explores AI muses that support human creativity through encouragement, critique, and reflection, generating substantial content when requested.

paragraphs: Possible You uses personalized stories and AI-generated portraits to help people imagine future career identities. The motivating problem is that possible careers can feel distant or abstract, especially when mentorship and resources are limited. The system turns career exploration into an encounter with representations of one’s possible future selves.

A mixed-methods study with 209 participants examines how people respond to these representations. The researchers find that perceived authenticity influences participants’ connection to their future selves. They also identify a difference between exploring several possibilities and concentrating on one: multiple selves broaden participants’ sense of possibility, while a single self encourages deeper commitment.

The findings highlight two different needs within career imagination: having room to discover alternatives and developing enough connection to commit to a direction. The system is framed as a reflective aid for shaping futures, rather than a means of predicting them. Its contribution is to make potential identities tangible and to show how the breadth of an AI-supported exploration relates to the depth of a participant’s engagement.
neurips-2025-possible-you-ai-generated-d.tldr: Possible You uses AI-generated future identities to support career reflection, revealing a trade-off between exploring possibilities and deepening commitment.

paragraphs: Prompt–Character Divergence, or PC-D, helps creators examine when a generated image resembles a known visual identity more than its prompt would suggest. The problem is distinguishing what a user requested from associations introduced by the model. The paper proposes a lightweight diagnostic that makes this relationship easier to inspect.

PC-D measures semantic drift and maps outputs along two axes: name proximity and model drift. These form a responsibility compass with four zones labeled model-driven risk, mixed attribution, safe co-creation, and user-driven intent. The map organizes different relationships between a prompt and the identities reflected in its output, giving creators a structure for self-auditing.

Evaluation across three open-source models and ten iconic characters finds drift patterns consistent with human judgment. The method also runs on consumer hardware, supporting its intended accessibility. The authors explicitly present it as a diagnostic rather than a resolution of attribution. Its value is in helping practitioners examine how their intentions and a model’s learned associations interact during visual creation.
neurips-2025-prompt-character-divergence.tldr: PC-D helps creators inspect whether generated images reflect prompted intent or additional associations with familiar visual identities.

paragraphs: Roulettective turns a vintage carousel slide projector into a physical interface for an AI-driven detective game. The project asks how an older artifact’s interaction mechanisms can support a new experience. Its starting point is the projector’s existing physical character and the possibilities that arise when those mechanisms are reprogrammed.

AI-generated narratives, visuals, and sound provide the material for the mystery-solving experience. Combined with the repurposed controls, these elements create a multimodal interface intended to be immersive, customizable, intuitive, and co-creative. The physical artifact and the generated content jointly shape the game, connecting tangible interaction with an adaptable fictional setting.

The broader design contribution is an approach the authors call AI repurposing. It treats interaction forms displaced by newer computing paradigms as resources for designing AI-driven physical interfaces. Roulettective serves as a concrete example of that approach, showing how a familiar but outdated object can acquire a new role. The paper presents this as a generalizable design framework grounded in learning from the legacies of older artifacts.
neurips-2025-roulettective-repurposing-a.tldr: Roulettective repurposes a vintage slide projector as a physical detective game powered by AI-generated stories, imagery, and sound.

paragraphs: SPICE addresses a practical problem in prompt-based image editing: detailed or local changes can damage the overall picture, sometimes after a single step. The paper introduces a training-free workflow intended to follow editing instructions while preserving regions the user has not asked to change. It also accepts arbitrary image resolutions and aspect ratios.

The workflow combines a base diffusion model with a Canny edge ControlNet model. This pairing brings the two models’ strengths together to handle free-form instructions. The authors report that SPICE can consistently improve image quality through more than one hundred editing steps while keeping unedited regions intact, making repeated refinement a central feature of the approach.

On a challenging dataset of realistic image-editing tasks, SPICE quantitatively outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and is consistently preferred by human annotators. These results support its usefulness for iterative editing that must balance requested changes with image preservation. The authors also release an implementation for popular diffusion-model web interfaces, making the workflow available for further research and artistic use.
neurips-2025-spice-a-synergistic-precise.tldr: SPICE combines diffusion and edge-based control for precise, repeated image editing while preserving unedited regions.
